purpose: Registry + intake gate for the standard-hull baseline fleet. Every record carries provenance (source/url/license/retrieval/verified) so a geometry file can be admitted only when its origin is stated and its sha256 is pinned.
honesty_note: This environment has no outbound network: no official IGES/offset file could be downloaded and no workshop page re-read. Literature particulars are entered offline (retrieval=offline_recollection, verified=false) and every unrecalled displacement volume is marked basis=closure (Cb*L*B*T) instead of being presented as a published value. What *is* machine-checked offline is arithmetic: G6b_reference_consistency requires a cited displacement to agree with the record's own Cb*L*B*T to 0.5 %, which is how the DTC beam transcription error was found and fixed.

ships.name: DTC

provenance.source: El Moctar, Shigunov, Zorn (2012) Duisburg Test Case: Post-Panamax Container Ship for Benchmarking. Ship Technology Research 59(3), 50-64

ships.notes: El Moctar, Shigunov & Zorn (2012) main particulars: Lpp 355.0 m, B 51.0 m, T 14.5 m, Cb 0.661, grad 173467 m^3. CORRECTED 2026-11-13 (round 2): this record previously carried B = 45.8 m with no cited displacement, so its reference was the closure Cb*L*B*T = 155834 m^3 and the error could not be seen. The cited volume 173467 m^3 (El Moctar et al. 2012) is reproduced to 0.0005 % by (L 355.0, B 51.0, T 14.5, Cb 0.661) and missed by 11.3 % by the old beam; L/B = 6.96 and B/T = 3.52 fit a post-Panamax container ship. G6b_reference_consistency now rejects the old quadruple (negative control mis_transcribed_particulars).
